summary: @servicetitan/hammer-react preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 728KB payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated with `_0xXXXX`-style identifiers and per-function string-lookup maps concealing values such as `"bun"`, `"--version"`, `"win32"`, and the Bun release URL. It downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<archive>.zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 728KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) whose strings are hidden behind a ~1200-entry cipher array (`n7gIxM`), a rotator (`WV8StW`), and a decoder (`hc1jfK9`); its contents are not human-readable. The payload is not referenced from any file under `dist/` (the actual React component library) and executes only via the preinstall alt-runtime path. A UI component library has no legitimate need to run install-time code, let alone under a separately-downloaded alternate runtime that Node-based scanners do not inspect. The combination of alt-runtime install-time execution + heavy obfuscation of both the loader and the payload + purpose mismatch with the advertised library is the alt-runtime-dropper attack shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
